questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the consequences of the Green Revolution?

options.text: Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment In cash to payment in kind (grain)
The rich grew richer and many of the poor stagnated or grew poorer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment In cash to payment in kind (grain) **__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Option 1** states that "Rising prices and a shift in the mode of payment of agricultural workers from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain)" is a consequence of the Green Revolution, which is not correct.
 
• The Green Revolution primarily focused on increasing agricultural productivity through the use of high-yield variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation.
 
• **Wages of agricultural workers increased** (Option 2) and **Employment of agricultural workers increased** (Option 3) are true outcomes of the Green Revolution.
 
• Option 4, **The rich grew richer and many of the poor stagnated or grew poorer**, is also a recognized consequence of the Green Revolution, as it often benefited wealthier farmers more than the poorer ones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Green Revolution was introduced in the 1960s and 1970s to combat food shortages in developing countries like India.
 
• It led to a significant increase in food grain production, particularly wheat and rice, through the adoption of new agricultural techniques and technologies.
 
• While it improved food security and reduced famine, it also resulted in socioeconomic disparities and environmental issues such as soil degradation and increased use of chemical fertilizers.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT regarding the Coriolis force?

options.text: It deflects the wind to the right in the north and left in the south.
It is absent at the equator.
Deflection is less when the speed of wind is high.
It is directly proportional to the angle of altitude

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deflection is less when the wind is high.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Coriolis force is an apparent force caused by the Earth's rotation.
 
• It deflects the wind to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere.
 
• It is absent at the equator because the Coriolis effect is zero there.
 
• The Coriolis force is proportional to the speed of the moving object and the sine of the latitude.
 
• Deflection is actually more when the wind speed is high, not less.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Coriolis force affects the direction of ocean currents and wind patterns, playing a crucial role in weather systems and climate.
 
• It is named after Gaspard-Gustave de Coriolis, a French scientist who described the effect in the 19th century.
 
• The Coriolis force is taken into account in meteorology, aviation, and oceanography for accurate predictions and navigation.
 
• In the absence of the Coriolis force, atmospheric and oceanic circulations would be significantly different, impacting the global climate system.

questions.question: At which place was the magnificent temple of Saiva constructed by the great Rashtrakuta King ‘Krishna I’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ellora**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The magnificent temple of Saiva was constructed by the great Rashtrakuta King 'Krishna I' at **Ellora**.
 
• Ellora is renowned for its monumental caves, which are a mix of Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
 
• The temple constructed by Krishna I is known as the **Kailasa temple**, which is one of the largest rock-cut ancient Hindu temples.
 
• The Kailasa temple is notable for its vertical excavation—carvers started at the top of the rock and excavated downward, which is a unique architectural feat.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Rashtrakuta dynasty ruled large parts of the Indian subcontinent between the 6th and 10th centuries.
 
• The Rashtrakutas are credited with some of the most significant contributions to art and architecture in India, including the Ellora Caves and the rock-cut temples at Badami.
 
• King Krishna I, who reigned from 756 to 774 CE, was a patron of art and architecture, and his reign saw the construction of the Kailasa temple at Ellora.
 
• The Ellora caves, including the Kailasa temple, are a testament to the religious tolerance during the Rashtrakuta period, as they encompass Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain monuments.
 
• The temple's construction reflects advanced knowledge of engineering and artistry, highlighting the Rashtrakutas' contributions to India's cultural heritage.

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: The British Government passed a law in the year 1856. It was meant for which among the following social reforms?

options.text: Abolition of Practice of Child Marriage
Law against Murdering of Female Child
Abolition of the Practice of Sati

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Widow Remarriage**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The British Government passed the Widow Remarriage Act in 1856.
 
• This act was a significant social reform aimed at improving the condition of widows in India.
 
• It allowed Hindu widows to remarry, which was previously prohibited by societal norms and religious practices.
 
• The act was championed by social reformers like Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who worked tirelessly to advocate for the rights of widows.
 
• The enactment of this law marked a progressive step towards gender equality and social justice in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Widow Remarriage Act of 1856 is also known as Act XV of 1856.
 
• This law was enacted during the tenure of Lord Dalhousie, the then Governor-General of India.
 
• The act was a result of the growing influence of the British colonial administration and reformist movements within Indian society.
 
• It played a crucial role in challenging the orthodox Hindu customs and paved the way for further social reforms in the country.
 
• Despite its enactment, widow remarriage faced significant resistance and took time to become widely accepted in society.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution states that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**51 A (e)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51 A (e)** of the Constitution of India states that 'It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.'
 
• This article is part of the **Fundamental Duties** enshrined in Part IVA of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens that while enjoying their rights, they must also be conscious of the duties they owe to their country and fellow citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Fundamental Duties** were inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and have been included to emphasize the obligations of citizens towards their nation.
 
• There are currently **eleven Fundamental Duties** listed in Article 51A of the Constitution.

questions.question: A circular coil having ‘n’ turns produces a field ______________ times large as that produced by a single turn
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**n**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A circular coil having **'n'** turns produces a field **n** times larger than that produced by a single turn.
 
• This is because the magnetic field produced by each turn of the coil adds up linearly when the turns are in series.
 
• Therefore, if a single turn produces a magnetic field of strength **B**, then **n** turns will produce a magnetic field of strength **nB**.
 
• This relationship is crucial in applications where stronger magnetic fields are required, such as in electromagnets and inductors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The strength of the magnetic field in a coil is also influenced by factors such as the current flowing through the coil and the core material used.
 
• Using a ferromagnetic core can significantly increase the magnetic field strength compared to an air core.
 
• The formula for the magnetic field strength at the center of a circular coil is given by **B = (μ₀ * n * I) / (2 * R)**, where **μ₀** is the permeability of free space, **n** is the number of turns, **I** is the current, and **R** is the radius of the coil.
